summary: ChatMessage: the two voices of an agent thread, as ONE item with TWO components and deliberately no bare <ChatMessage>. The sheet's own Gaps row asked for that and §7a's Sheet-and-Drawer test agrees — the receiver has no bubble by design, so a `role` prop would carry a bubble, an attachment slot and a status caption that mean nothing in half its uses, and an actions row, a caret and a failure block that mean nothing in the other half. Sender: right-aligned bg-elevated bubble, radius-lg, no tail, no border, no avatar, no timestamp inside; attachments above the text INSIDE the bubble; delivery state carried entirely by a caption, because the bubble's fill never moves — asserted as a sameness, which is the assertion that fails if anyone tints it. Receiver: no container at all, leading-relaxed against the sender's leading-normal (asserted as an ORDERING, not two numbers), a static caret while streaming, and the actions row WITHHELD rather than hidden while it streams — a hidden row is six tab stops in front of an unfinished answer. The row is revealed by hover AND focus-within AND forced visible under `@media (hover:none)`: three channels, because dropping any one strands a keyboard or a touch user. THE WIDTH CAP IS A CUSTOM PROPERTY, NOT A PROP. The sheet's rule (75% at 640, 85% once the column narrows) is about the COLUMN, and no viewport breakpoint describes a 308px sidebar inside a 1440px window — so `--ui-chat-message-bubble-max-width` is declared on the root at 75% and the app that chose the column moves it. It is also not the same axis as `size`: the sheet draws a 343px mobile column at `md` with the narrow cap. TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE DRAWING, both pushed back into Paper. The failed caption reads "Not sent — retry" in the sheet; a word inside a caption cannot be tabbed to and announces as prose, so retry ships as a real Button and the sheet has been redrawn (both schemes). The failure block is a tighter Banner with an action — Banner is p-lg, has no action slot, and uses --ui-intent-danger-fg where this uses the deeper --ui-text-on-danger-subtle — so it ships as a local recipe with the third-inline-alert observation recorded in needsDesign. Geometry spec covers both voices, and the receiver case is the one worth having: a track with no inset, no fill and no corner, held together by 12px.
